thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING — prod streaming: decode-runtime.p99 spike in eu-west-1 (streaming). auto-detect: streaming-tail stalls + increased page faults. link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/decode-runtime/d/streaming

alex: oncall here, looking. pulling p95/p99 now.

alex: p95 baseline ~ 120ms -> 650ms, p99 baseline ~ 420ms -> 2.3s. streaming tail sessions showing repeated stalls up to 45s. CPU on host not high, GPU memory pressure + kernel page fault rate up.

maria: any recent rollouts in that region?

ryan (eng-runtime): yep we deployed trt8.2 + flashattn-v1.4 kernel variant last night 02:15 UTC to eu-west canary. small percentage. also landed a compile-path change that toggles dynamic-kv-alloc + USE_FLASHATTN=1.

sre_jordan: seeing a correlated bump in page-eviction counters on nodes with new kernel. likely compilepath / kernel interaction causing heavier page thrash for long streaming sessions.

alex: grabbing logs from a stalled session — posting snippet:
```
[2026-03-12T02:43:12Z] stream-id=xyz decode: wait_for_kv_cache: page_fault -> stall 1345ms
[2026-03-12T02:43:12Z] kernel: evicting kv pages, pinned_pages=0, candidate_pages=12
[2026-03-12T02:43:13Z] trt: flashattn kernel fallback triggered (slow path)
[2026-03-12T02:43:57Z] stream-id=xyz decode: resumed after swap, latency=44.3s
```

maria: sounds like paging-induced tail. do we have a quick mitigation?

infra-lead: immediate options: (1) rollback trt/flashattn kernel variant in eu-west canary -> full, (2) flip compile flag to disable flashattn fastpath (DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1) via rollout, (3) move streaming traffic to legacy pool without new kernel.

ryan (eng-runtime): I recommend option 2 + 3 as fast path. flipping flag is config-only and affects new alloc path; routing traffic to legacy pool reduces blast radius. rollback of driver will take longer (node drain).

alex: I'll start a targeted route split to move 30% of streaming to legacy-pool-eu while we flip the flag.

alex: k8s patch I used:
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env ds/decode-runtime RUNTIME_KERNEL_FLAG=legacy-compile-20260301 --selector=pool=legacy-pool-eu
kubectl rollout restart ds/decode-runtime -n inference --field-selector=spec.nodeSelector.pool=legacy-pool-eu
```

maria: I'll stage the config flip (DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1) in canary for 5m then promote. ryan, please watch for paging counters.

ryan (eng-runtime): watching. set alert thresholds lowered. initial canary shows p99 back down to ~600–800ms for the disabled fastpath. good sign.

incident-bot: EVENT UPDATE — routing change applied. canary config flip started by maria.

ana (customer-ops): heads-up: 3 customers (two enterprise, one PLG) reported degraded streaming responses ~02:40 UTC. one customer saw session disconnects. I've opened a ticket and linked affected request ids.

alex: noted. tagging customer-ops and PS for follow-up. sending apology + incident summary when we have mitigation confirmed.

sre_jordan: post-mitigation metrics: p95 ~ 170ms, p99 ~ 900ms for canary nodes. legacy-pool running steady. page-fault rate dropped ~78% on those nodes.

maria: rolling config to remaining nodes now. ETA ~ 6m.

infra-lead: plan after config roll: run a controlled driver/kernel rollback on a subset of nodes and validate with long-running streaming load (12h soak) before full driver revert. also create a guardrail that pins future compilepath merges until we have regression test for long streaming sessions.

ryan (eng-runtime): filed PR to add streaming-tail e2e test targeting KV cache durability under high sequence lengths. PR: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/4521

alex: customer remediation note drafted. will send once rollout complete.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigation in progress -> severity lowered to P2 (customer impact contained).

ana (customer-ops): customers notified. one asked for ETA on fix; said will update after full rollout.

maria: rollout finished across eu-west ~03:05 UTC. monitoring for 30m. preliminary look stable.

sre_jordan: p99 trending down, streaming tail exceptions mostly gone. closing loop: root cause likely an interaction between new flashattn kernel fast path + compile-time kv allocation changes that increased transient working set, causing excessive GPU page churn for long-lived streaming sessions.

infra-lead: follow-ups: 1) revert compile flag from main until tests land, 2) add alert for page-eviction-to-latency correlation, 3) schedule kernel/driver rollback plan if further regressions.

alex: oncall handoff to maria in 45m. leaving notes in incident ticket.

maria: taking handoff. I'll watch eu-west for next 2h and coordinate postmortem. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED -> mitigation verified, customer notifications sent. postmortem assigned to eng-runtime (ryan) + infra (infra-lead) + oncall (alex) — ticket #INC-2026-314.
